title: Liability during negotiations
summary: Negotiations can create limited legal obligations before the parties form the final contract they are discussing. The obligation may arise from a specific assurance or an agreement about how to negotiate.
notes:
First determine whether a complete agreement already exists, with a writing intended only as a later record. If it does not, identify the narrower undertaking actually made. Dixon concerns assurances and alleged reliance during loan-modification discussions. Cyberchron concerns work performed while major commercial terms remained unresolved. Channel Home Centers examines a letter promising withdrawal from the market and good-faith negotiation.

A duty to negotiate in good faith does not guarantee that negotiations will succeed. A reliance claim likewise does not automatically entitle the claimant to the profits of the hoped-for final bargain. The assurance, reasonable induced action, causation, and applicable remedy must each be established. The assigned French Civil Code provision supplies a comparative rule protecting freedom to negotiate while requiring good faith and limiting recovery for faulty negotiations. Keep that provision’s jurisdiction and remedy limits distinct from the American cases.

topics.precontractual-liability: Specific preliminary commitments can have consequences before a final bargain.
